why: The markers run 60, 59, 60. The step back breaks the sequence, so the report gets no range and the rows under the first 60 get no column. The last row starts after the 59 marker, and the 60 after it confirms 59, so it takes 59 as printed.

Title:ADMISSION FROM CHINA OF WIVES OF SINGAPORE RESIDENTS
MPs Speaking:Mr Lim Yew Hock (Minister for Labour and Welfare); Mr Lim Cher Kheng;


Column: 60

ADMISSION FROM CHINA OF WIVES OF SINGAPORE RESIDENTS


    3. Mr Lim Cher Kheng asked the Minister for Labour and Welfare whether he will supply the following information regarding the admission from China of wives of Singapore residents : -

    (a) the number of applications (i) approved and (ii) rejected during (1) the period JuneDecember 1955, and (2) the first two months of 1956;

    (b) the number of applications (1) received and (2) still outstanding during (i) JulyDecember 1952, (ii) JanuaryJune 1953, (iii) July-December 1953, (iv) January-June 1954, (v) July-December 1954, (vi) January-June 1955; and whether he is satisfied with the speed with which these applications are cleared.

    Mr Lim Yew Hock: It is not possible without very considerable work to give exact figures. The figures which follow are approximate only : - 

(a)                               Approved     Rejected

      July-December 1955           1,600          200

      January-February 1956          600           60

(b)                               Received    Outstanding

      July-December 1952           2,000           30

      January-June 1953            1,700           80

      July-December 1953           1,800          160

      January-June 1954            1,300          300

      July-December 1954           1,400          380

      January-June 1955            1,550          620


Column: 59



    The Immigration Department have engaged additional staff to deal with these outstanding cases, the majority of which are under active consideration and will shortly be finalised. For the remainder, the Department is writing to the sponsors to produce further evidence. In new cases, the sponsor is called for interview within one month of filing the application, and, provided that the

Column: 60

evidence produced at that time is satisfactory, the entry permit is issued within a further one month period. Unfortunately, despite detailed instructions many sponsors fail to produce satisfactory evidence at the first interview and thus delay their own cases. I am satisfied with the steps being taken both to clear the old outstanding cases and also to deal with new applications.
